title: Account recovery, the back door
brief: 18:00. A text arrives with a password reset code you never asked for. Someone is trying to reset your account.
insight: An attacker does not need your password if they can reset it. The reset goes wherever your recovery options point.
teaches: A reset code you did not ask for means someone is at your account's back door
Remove recovery emails, numbers and questions you no longer control
Never read a code out to anyone, even a caller who seems to be IT

value.label: Old personal email
value.note: You stopped using this in 2023, and its password was in a breach last year.

value.label: Recovery phone
value.note: Your old number. You switched phones and networks last spring.

value.label: Security questions
value.value: Name of your first pet? Your mother's maiden name?
value.note: Both answers are on your public profile.

from.name: Veltrix
details: Veltrix's own sign in service sends reset codes from this sender.

messages.text: Veltrix: your password reset code is {{code}}. If you did not ask for this, someone may be trying to reset your password. Never share this code.

setup.title: Messages
setup.body: Veltrix: your password reset code is...

outcome.label: Read your sign in activity
outcome.what: A password reset was started from {{place}}, through your old personal email.
outcome.ideal: checks sign in activity when a reset code arrives unasked.

outcome.label: Opened your recovery options
outcome.what: Three of them point at things you no longer control.
outcome.ideal: reviews recovery options, not just the password.

outcome.label: Removed the old personal email
outcome.what: That address was breached. Whoever controls it could reset your work account.
outcome.ideal: removes recovery emails it no longer uses.

outcome.label: Removed the old phone number
outcome.what: Old numbers get recycled to strangers. A reset text would go to them.
outcome.ideal: keeps only numbers it still owns.

outcome.label: Removed the security questions
outcome.what: Anyone can answer them from your public profile. They are a password written in public.
outcome.ideal: does not rely on security questions with public answers.

outcome.label: Would not read out the code
outcome.what: The caller ID said Priya, but caller ID can be faked. The code is the key to your account.
outcome.ideal: never shares a code with a caller, whoever the screen says they are.

outcome.label: Changed your password
outcome.what: Every other session is signed out, and the half finished reset is dead.
outcome.ideal: changes the password after a reset attempt.

outcome.label: Read a reset code to a caller
outcome.what: Caller ID can be faked. A reset code is the key to the account.
outcome.ideal: never reads a code to anyone who calls.

decide.objective: Someone is trying to reset your account. Shut the back door.
decide.insight: Recovery options are a second set of keys. Old email, old numbers and guessable questions are keys other people may be holding.

hint.text: Open Account security. Read Sign in activity, then open Recovery and remove the old email, the old phone number and the security questions. Do not read the code to anyone.

script.say: Hi Sam, it is IT. We can see someone trying to reset your password. To block it, I need the code we just texted you. Can you read it out?

choices.label: IT never needs my codes. I will call the service desk myself.

script.say: Perfect, that is blocked now. Have a good evening.

outcome.label: Read the reset code to the caller
outcome.what: That code finished the reset. The attacker now owns your Veltrix account and has locked you out.
outcome.ideal: never reads a code to a caller, whoever the caller ID says.

card.title: The code was the key
body: The caller was the attacker, with Priya's name spoofed onto the caller ID. The reset code you read out was the last thing they needed.
IT never needs your codes. And the reset only worked because an old, breached personal email was still listed as a recovery option.
card.ideal: keeps codes to itself and removes recovery options it no longer controls.
card.rewindLabel: Rewind to before I read it out

outcome.label: Closed every stale recovery route
outcome.what: Only your work mailbox and your authenticator can reset the account now.
outcome.ideal: keeps recovery options to things it controls today.

card.title: The back door is shut
body: The reset was coming through your old personal email, breached last year. Your old phone number and your public security answers were two more ways in.
Now only your work mailbox and your authenticator can get into the account. Change the password and report the attempt.
card.ideal: reviews recovery options the moment a reset code arrives unasked.

auto.text: Change your password, and report the reset attempt.

hint.text: In Account security change your password, then raise a Helpdesk ticket (my account may be compromised).

outcome.label: Reported the reset attempt
outcome.what: IT can block the reset and check whether anyone else was targeted.
